WiFi hotspots. Phones that do have GPS turned on report home with the location of hot spots. Other phones report the hotspot name and a reverse lookup gives the location.

Cell tower triangulation also is fairly accurate.

WiFi gives better contextual information though. Makes for more targeted ads or other purposes.
How when you are out in middle of a national forest with zero wifi hotspots, though? And if its thru cell tower - how location but not service?

Service requires two way communication. Towers are much more sensitive at listening for phones than phones are at listening for towers. When your phone is on but not connected, it constantly sends out a message soliciting a response from a cell tower so that it can initiate service. Technically this allows for limited triangulation without service. This is also why your phone's battery will drain faster than normal. Amps are cranked to max input/output as it constantly solicits a response.

If you're so far away there are no towers then you can't passively be tracked.

Did I read that right - when out of service the phone is constantly trying to ping the towers which drains the battery faster - so battery life doesn't last as long when out of service?

Also, thanks.

I'm making some assumptions about your phone. But in general that is correct. Some phones don't vary their power. But most modern phones do. They increase and decrease power input/output based on signal strength and signal to noise ratios. When it doesn't hear a response it cranks up max tx power for a tower to hear it. Likewise, it has to crank up its rx amplifiers to amplify any response which might be returned. The result is a higher power draw until it makes a connection.

This is why carrying your phone in your pant pocket can drain your battery faster than having it on the desk next to you. This assumes it would otherwise have a stronger connection while on your desk.
